title: SNS Delivery Failures and Bounce/Complaint

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatch` events with `namespace="AWS/SNS" metric_name="NumberOfNotificationsFailed"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.37 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatch` traffic without `namespace="AWS/SNS" metric_name="NumberOfNotificationsFailed"`. Confirm UC-4.1.37 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

value: On AWS, detecting 'SNS Delivery Failures and Bounce/Complaint' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.1.37 drives high-priority fault alerting before customer-impacting drift.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect SNS metrics. Alert when NumberOfNotificationsFailed > 0. For email subscriptions, enable bounce/complaint feedback and ingest via SNS or EventBridge. Track delivery success rate.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/SNS" metric_name="NumberOfNotificationsFailed"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.37_sns_delivery_failures_an_37"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect sns delivery failures and bounce/complaint. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_37_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (failures by topic), Table (topic, failure count), Single value (failed notifications)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of sns delivery failures and bounce/complaint so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
